text:
maria.chen: Heads up — we started seeing a correlated rise in streaming token latencies for us-west-2-gpupool ~9:12am UTC, p99 jumps +120ms and a bunch of client RPC deadline misses.
raj: saw that too, looks like bursts rather than steady increase. Any packet loss on the infra dashboards?
ops-bot: Alert: token-streaming-latency high on us-west-2-gpupool (nodes: gpu-usw2-a{12..18})
maria.chen: No significant DROP counters on the top-of-rack, but tcp retransmits are up on a subset of hosts.
dylan: can we get a tcpdump from one of the affected servers + sibling pod host? reordering usually shows up as out-of-order seqs.
ingrid: capturing now, will put sample on /tmp/pcap and upload to shared bucket. quick grep shows a lot of dup acks and out-of-order segments.
raj: check MTU/GSO/GRO settings — last time we had a similar tail problem it was a jumbo/fragmentation mismatch after a kernel update.
ingrid: running `ip link show` and `ethtool -k` on node gpu-usw2-a15:
```
2: eth0: mtu 9000 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
    features: tx-checksumming rx-checksumming tcp-segmentation-offload generic-segmentation-offload large-receive-offload
Intel X710, GSO: on, GRO: on, LRO: off
```
maria.chen: that looks normal. but pcap shows large packets being split by intermediate switch into smaller frames and reassembled at host causing out-of-order arrival to guests.
raj: could be path MTU discovery failing for some flows, or an ECMP path taking a link with different MTU/DSCP handling. any recent changes on leaf switches in the rack?
ops-bot: Deploy event: qos-policy-2026-03-17 applied to rack-westcoast-14 at 08:55 UTC.
dylan: that qos change touched L2/L3 counters — possible config drift. I suspect GSO segmentation happening on host, switch doesn't preserve ordering when it fragments across ports.
ingrid: here's a snippet from the pcap showing reordering: `seq 1001..1500` followed by `seq 501..1000` arriving later.
maria.chen: streaming RPCs are sensitive because we stream tokens over a long-lived HTTP/2/gRPC channel; reorders cause head-of-line and increased decode latency.
raj: short-term mitigation: disable GSO/GRO on affected hosts to force segmentation in kernel before NIC. lower throughput but should reduce reorders.
dylan: agree. I'd also add a tc fq_codel on the egress to smooth bursts and avoid deep queues at the switch.
ingrid: I'm rolling a canary change to two nodes: `/sbin ethtool -K eth0 gso off gro off tso off` then monitor.
maria.chen: please also add a temporary routing rule to prefer single-path for critical pods while we triage (no ECMP fanout).
raj: noted. creating a maintenance tag and will mark capacity as degraded for autoscaler to avoid scheduling new streaming tasks there.
sre-oncall: I put a pager note for oncall, and bumped alert to P1 if deadline misses exceed 1% for 15m.
dylan: if disabling offloads doesn't help, next step is to push an XDP program to preserve ordering or enable host-side segmentation (skb->skb linearize), but that's higher risk.
ingrid: can confirm canary nodes show immediate drop in out-of-order events after offloads off. latency p95 back to normal, p99 trending down.
maria.chen: great. timeline: canary change 09:35, observed improvement 09:40. plan to rollback qos-policy on rack-westcoast-14 with network team if we can't find a safe path.
raj: filing a follow-up to audit switch MTU and TC configs, and run a synthetic long-lived stream test across all racks.
maria.chen: thanks all — keep updates here. tagging @networking-team for visibility.
ops-bot: Note: maintenance window scheduled for 10:15 UTC to validate MTU on leaf switches in rack-westcoast-14.
maria.chen: after maintenance we'll either re-enable GSO/GRO and validate, or keep offload disabled until switch firmware/config fixed. we should also add unit test to our canary pipeline that simulates fragmentation/reorder to catch regressions.
raj: added to infra backlog. closing loop once network team confirms config parity. :thumbsup:
